page_title: (Draft) Mitigating the Risk of Software Vulnerabilities by Adopting a Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF)

summary.title: Mitigating the Risk of Software Vulnerabilities by Adopting a Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF) (Draft)
summary.one_liner: NIST draft white paper recommending a high-level Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF) of practices, grouped into Prepare, Protect, Produce and Respond, to add to any SDLC model.
keywords: how to reduce vulnerabilities in released software
takeaways: An SSDF is a set of high-level secure development practices meant to be added to any SDLC model such as waterfall, agile or DevOps.
Practices are organized into four groups: Prepare the Organization (PO), Protect the Software (PS), Produce Well-Secured Software (PW), and Respond to Vulnerability Reports (RV).
Each practice has a statement, tasks, implementation examples, and references to other established secure development standards.
The framework is deliberately tool- and technology-neutral, so organizations can implement it with manual or automated processes.
Software producers can use it to improve their development, and software consumers can reuse it in acquisition requirements.
summary.summary: This NIST cybersecurity white paper (June 2019 public draft) argues that secure development practices must be added to any SDLC model, since few models address security in detail. It defines a Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF) of high-level practices organized into four groups: Prepare the Organization, Protect the Software, Produce Well-Secured Software, and Respond to Vulnerability Reports. Each practice lists tasks, implementation examples, and mappings to referenced standards such as BSIMM, ISO 27034, and NIST SP 800-53. The paper is intended as a common vocabulary for business owners, developers, acquirers, and security staff, and it does not prescribe specific tools.
